policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'even as Christ also loved you' renders ὑμᾶς; the base ἡμᾶς would give 'loved us'.
ASV 'and gave himself up for us' renders ἡμῶν, and its note 'Some ancient authorities read you' maps explicitly to WH's ὑμῶν.
The readings differ only in the order of ἀκαθαρσία and πᾶσα; English fixes the quantifier before the noun, so ASV 'all uncleanness' renders either.
ASV 'which are not befitting' fits both the relative clause ἃ οὐκ ἀνῆκεν and RP's substantival participle τὰ οὐκ ἀνήκοντα, which English also renders with a relative.
ASV 'For this ye know of a surety' renders two verbs of knowing, ἴστε and γινώσκοντες; RP's periphrastic ἐστε γινώσκοντες is a single 'ye know' and leaves nothing for the unitalicized 'of a surety'.
The readings differ only in the gender of the relative, ὅ or ὅς; English takes 'who' from the personal antecedent 'covetous man' either way.
ASV 'for the fruit of the light' renders φωτός; RP's πνεύματος would give 'the fruit of the Spirit'.
ASV 'Look therefore carefully how ye walk' puts ἀκριβῶς with βλέπετε, matching the base order; the RP order attaches it to the walking, as in 'see how circumspectly ye walk'.
ASV 'but understand what the will of the Lord is' is imperative, rendering συνίετε; RP's participle συνιέντες would give 'understanding'.
The readings differ only in ἐν before ψαλμοῖς; English supplies a preposition for the bare dative too, so ASV 'in psalms' renders either.
The readings differ only in ἐν before τῇ καρδίᾳ; English supplies a preposition for the bare dative too, so ASV 'with your heart' renders either.
ASV 'Wives, be in subjection unto your own husbands' italicizes 'be in subjection', marking a supplied verb; both RP's ὑποτάσσεσθε and Treg's ὑποτασσέσθωσαν would supply one in the source.
ASV 'being himself the saviour of the body' italicizes 'being', so no ἐστιν stood in the source, and it has no connective for RP's added καί.
ὡς and ὥσπερ are the comparative particle with and without the intensive -περ; ASV 'But as the church is subject to Christ' renders either.
ASV 'be to their husbands' renders the bare article τοῖς with a possessive, as it does at 5:33 'her husband'; RP's ἰδίοις would add 'own', which ASV writes wherever ἴδιος stands (5:22, 5:28).
ASV 'Husbands, love your wives' has no 'own'; RP's ἑαυτῶν would give 'your own wives', as ASV renders ἑαυτῶν at 5:28.

ASV 'present the church to himself a glorious church' takes τὴν ἐκκλησίαν as the object and italicizes the predicate 'church'; RP's αὐτήν would furnish the object pronoun and leave the predicate noun unsupplied.
ASV 'Even so ought husbands also to love' has an unitalicized 'also' rendering καί, which RP omits.
ASV 'even as Christ also the church' renders Χριστός; RP's κύριος would give 'the Lord'.
ASV 'because we are members of his body' ends the verse there; RP's added ἐκ τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῶν ὀστέων αὐτοῦ would give 'of his flesh and of his bones'.
The readings differ only in the article τόν before πατέρα; ASV 'his father' takes its possessive from the kinship noun either way.

ASV 'his father' is unitalicized, but ASV renders a bare article with an unitalicized possessive in this chapter (5:24 'their husbands', 5:33 'her husband'), so it does not show whether RP's αὐτοῦ stood in the source.
The readings differ only in the article τήν before μητέρα; ASV 'and mother' is identical either way.
προσκολληθήσεται takes its complement as a bare dative or with πρός; English 'cleave to his wife' needs the same 'to' for either.
